A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same ShifCon paper, with 23 pages including Appendix sections A.1-A.7. Complete text comparison and rendered-page inspection support reliable comparison of the text, figures, tables and equations.

before.justification: v3 reports original multilingual benchmark evaluations, component ablations and representation analyses in Section 3 and the appendices, including detailed per-language results.

after.justification: v5 retains these original benchmark results, ablations and representation analyses, including the detailed appendix results.

M1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix A.4 retain the same shift projections, subspace-based layer selection, contrastive objective, two-stage training and language-vector updates. The two corrected method-name spellings denote the same procedure.

E1.justification: Training retains MGSM8KInstruct and the same Bactrian-X language subset. Evaluation retains MGSM, FLORES, XCOPA, XNLI and XStoryCloze with identical language and task coverage (Section 3.1; Appendix A.3).

E2.justification: English-only fine-tuning, MSFT and AFP remain the same comparators in the corresponding experiments. Correcting '+ShiftCon' to '+ShifCon' in Tables 1 and 2 does not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: The zero-shot MGSM and four-shot remaining evaluations, accuracy and ChrF++ metrics, model configurations, prompts and training settings are unchanged (Section 3.1; Appendices A.3-A.4).

E4.justification: Both versions contain identical layer-selection sensitivity tests, shift/MCL ablations, language-consistency analysis, representation visualizations, and training-stage and pooling comparisons (Section 3.3; Appendices A.1 and A.4).

E5.justification: Appendix A.4 already reports averaging experiments over three different random seeds, and v5 retains that statement unchanged. Existing graphical uncertainty displays, including Figure 3's standard-deviation band, are also unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and graphical findings remain unchanged, including Appendix A.5's per-language results. For example, Table 1 retains ShifCon's Llama-2 7B MGSM high/low-resource scores of 48.2/35.1; only its row-label spelling changes.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations in Section 2, the subspace-distance details in Appendix A.2, and the language-vector estimation derivation in Appendix A.4 are identical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements and conclusion retain identical claims about improving non-dominant languages through ShifCon, selecting suitable layers and generalizing across model families and scales.

C2.justification: The interpretations concerning information aggregation, representation alignment and language-specific information are unchanged. Section 6 retains the same limitations concerning parallel corpora, models up to 7.5B parameters and unexplored architectures.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures remain identical, including four A100 GPUs, hyperparameters, optimization settings, evaluation templates and language-vector updates. The code-availability statement and repository address are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 4, citations throughout the paper and the reference list are unchanged. No cited works or substantive positioning relative to prior research are added or removed.

P1.justification: v5 adds Feng Yao and the University of California, San Diego affiliation, adjusts affiliation numbering and updates the arXiv version/date header. It also corrects '+ShiftCon' to '+ShifCon' in Tables 1 and 2; prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The shortened method labels make Tables 1 and 2 slightly narrower and adjust their horizontal spacing. Figures, captions, table organization and placements otherwise remain unchanged; every appendix page is visually identical.

improvement.justification: The two table-label corrections provide small editorial consistency gains, alongside updated author and header information. Methods, evidence, explanations, reproducibility information and limitations remain identical throughout the main text and appendices, establishing no meaningful net change in overall paper quality.
